categories.hint: inference serving: KV cache, continuous batching, quantisation, vector indexes, RAG retrieval, GPU scheduling, context windows, embedding drift
consensus and coordination: Raft, leader election, quorums, split brain, partitioning, replication lag, exactly-once vs at-least-once
storage engines: B-trees vs LSM, MVCC, WAL, isolation levels, query planners, index selectivity, vacuum, hot partitions
the wire: TCP slow start, TLS handshakes, HTTP/2 vs 3, head-of-line blocking, DNS resolution, BGP, anycast, load balancer algorithms
cache behaviour: invalidation strategies, thundering herd, stampede locks, TTL jitter, write-through vs write-back, CDN tiering, cache keys
parallel execution: locks and contention, async runtimes, event loops, backpressure, queue depth, thread pools, false sharing
where the time goes: p99 vs mean, tail amplification, GC pauses, cold starts, memory layout, cache lines, N+1 queries, profiling
real attack surface: token lifetimes, JWT pitfalls, TLS termination, secret rotation, supply-chain, SSRF, rate limit bypass
seeing production: distributed tracing, metric cardinality explosions, sampling strategies, SLOs and error budgets, log costs
the platform: container cold start, k8s scheduling and evictions, autoscaling lag, blue-green vs canary, IaC drift, noisy neighbours
data in motion: streaming vs batch, backfills, schema evolution, watermarks, idempotent consumers, partition skew, CDC
when it breaks: retry storms, circuit breakers, idempotency keys, graceful degradation, timeouts and deadlines, incident patterns
finding the cause: bisecting, core dumps, flame graphs, heisenbugs, strace/dtrace, reproducing race conditions, reading a stack trace properly
writing code that survives: naming, boundaries, coupling, dependency inversion, when abstraction costs more than duplication, deleting code
proving it works: test pyramids vs trophies, flaky tests, property-based testing, contract tests, fixtures vs factories, mutation testing
the tools under your hands: git internals (objects, packfiles, reflog), rebase vs merge semantics, bisect, monorepo builds, caching in CI
what the kernel is doing: page faults, context switches, file descriptors, epoll, memory mapping, signals, cgroups, syscall cost
how your code becomes machine code: JIT warmup, inlining, branch prediction, vectorisation, undefined behaviour, linking, dead code elimination
algorithms where they actually bite: hash collisions in the wild, big-O lying about constants, bloom filters, consistent hashing, sorting at scale
decisions you defend later: monolith vs services, event-driven tradeoffs, API versioning, ADRs, strangler migrations, build vs buy
the bill as an engineering constraint: egress pricing, idle GPU burn, over-provisioned clusters, log retention, storage tiers, cost per request
the craft around the code: design reviews, RFC writing, on-call practice, estimating, mentoring, reading unfamiliar codebases fast, interview system design
